Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates dextrocardia (heart apex pointing to the right) and bronchiectatic changes (ring shadows and tram-tracking) predominantly at the lung bases, which are classic radiological features of Kartagener's syndrome (a subset of primary ciliary dyskinesia characterized by the triad of situs inversus, chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis).
